task.pr_title: Parallelize bulk facets & word prefix fid/position docids

cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description:
The source database is serialized as `word, 0, position -> docids`, which means it will be ordered as below:
```
he, 0, 0 -> [docids]
he, 0, 1 -> [docids]
he, 0, 2 -> [docids]
hell, 0, 0 -> [docids]
hell, 0, 1 -> [docids]
hell, 0, 2 -> [docids]
hello, 0, 0 -> [docids]
hello, 0, 1 -> [docids]
hello, 0, 2 -> [docids]
heritage, 0, 0 -> [docids]
heritage, 0, 1 -> [docids]
heritage, 0, 2 -> [docids]
```

Meaning that for the prefix `h`, it would create more than one `PrefixIntegerEntry` per position:

```rust
PrefixIntegerEntry { prefix: "h", pos: 0, .. } // he, 0, 0
PrefixIntegerEntry { prefix: "h", pos: 1, .. } // he, 0, 1 : because we changed position
PrefixIntegerEntry { prefix: "h", pos: 2, .. } // he, 0, 2 : because we changed position
PrefixIntegerEntry { prefix: "h", pos: 0, .. } // hell, 0, 0 : we come back to position 0 and we push the same PrefixIntegerEntry as the first one but with different docids.
...
```

then when writing into the database, we iterate over the indexes `for PrefixIntegerEntry { prefix, pos, serialized_length } in index` and override the value.

I think the persisted value for each prefixes will only contain the  `docids` of the last word starting with the prefix for each position.
In our example, we would only have the `heritage` docids for the `h` prefix.

Am I right, or am I missing something? 🤔

evidence.thread_resolution:
Kerollmops: I may be wrong but the databases we are iterating on are `word_prefix_fid_docids` and `word_position_docids` which are of type `Database<StrBEU16Codec, CboRoaringBitmapCodec>` which means that the key is not composed of the zero you are showing in the middle, right?
Kerollmops: Ok, we discussed and the bug is indeed here. What I plan to do to fix it is to collect all the bitmaps under their positions for a given prefix in an hashmap.
